title: Cause-and-effect logic (because / since / so / led to)
subtitle: Words in Context · 29 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **29 of the official questions in Words in Context are this one** — 20 Easy, 7 Medium, 2 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The blank sits inside a reason clause or a result clause, marked by words such as 'because', 'since', 'for this reason', 'so', 'thus', or a phrase saying one thing led to another.
- The choices are often verbs of change (increase, reduce, cause, block) or adjectives that describe a process.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) State the chain in plain words: X happens, so Y.
- 2) Ask which word has to fill the blank for the chain to make sense physically or logically.
- 3) Eliminate choices that reverse the direction or describe a different kind of effect.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You pick a verb that goes in the right general direction but acts on the wrong thing, such as 'hides' when the text needs 'reduces'.
You can also get the direction backwards because the causal chain has two steps.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You pick a verb that goes in the right general direction but acts on the wrong thing, such as 'hides' when the text needs 'reduces'.
